provenance: Computed by the LunarWindow pipeline from NASA LOLA terrain and NASA SPICE (DE421) ephemerides. Code written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified by the team with automated tests and a comparison against NASA PGDA illumination maps.
verdict: Touchdown 2029-07-24T01 UTC: the Sun's centre is 0.09 deg above the skyline and the top of Earth's disc 0.05 deg above the skyline (power and a link at landing).
Over 14 days: Sun up 97%, Earth in view 98%, both 96% of the time.
Survives the mission: the battery never drops below 140 Wh (lowest 617 Wh).
Longest darkness 5 h: that is the cold soak.
Battery used on this mission: 83 Wh of the 560 Wh it can use above its 140 Wh floor.
Battery model: power = panel power x visible Sun, whatever the Sun's direction (a sun-tracking array), so survival is an upper bound for fixed panels.
why: Marginal touchdown: the Sun's centre and the top of Earth's disc clears the skyline by under 0.5 deg; the Sun is 0.09 deg above the skyline (bearing 177 deg, set by terrain 10 m away at 0.45 deg), so there is almost no margin for a landing error, a lower antenna or a later hour.
Darkest spell from 2029-08-05T08 UTC (5 h): terrain 10.1 km away blocks it (bearing 26 deg: skyline 1.20 deg, centre of the body at 1.18 deg).
Longest Earth blackout from 2029-08-06T18 UTC (7 h): it is below the Moon's own curvature (bearing 148 deg, horizon -1.31 deg).
